items.content: Jessica Martinez works from home most days. Her international business travel to Tokyo, Japan is now confirmed — she will attend a conference there, traveling January 15–22. (Earlier this was only tentative, for December or January.)

Jessica Marie Martinez holds a US passport (number 487223901) that is an ePassport with a chip, issued in 2015. It expires on February 18th, 2025 — just under a month after her confirmed Tokyo trip return (Jan 22, 2025), which is a very tight buffer. Delta strongly advised her to renew it before travel; airlines sometimes check passport validity more strictly. She can update her passport number with Delta up to 72 hours before departure. She still plans to renew by mail via Form DS-82.

Jessica Martinez plans to renew her US passport by mail using Form DS-82 (eligible: passport undamaged, issued when 16 or older, issued within last 15 years). For mail renewal she must include: the completed DS-82, current passport, a new photo, and payment by check or money order (payable to "US Department of State") — credit cards are only accepted for in-person applications. She plans to get her passport photo at CVS. Expedited processing costs $190 total ($130 renewal fee + $60 expedited). Originally she planned to wait until the Japan trip was confirmed, but the trip is now booked (Jan 15–22, 2025), so renewal timing is more urgent — she should submit well before travel (early October was the recommended deadline to have it by December).

Details relevant to Jessica Martinez's passport renewal: Expedited mail applications go to National Passport Processing Center, PO Box 90955, Philadelphia, PA 19190-0955. Application status can be tracked online at travel.state.gov. If she needs urgent processing (travel within 14 days), the nearest passport agency to her is in Los Angeles at 11000 Wilshire Blvd, Suite 1000 (appointments mandatory). Passport photos must be 2x2 inches, white background, taken within the last 6 months, with a neutral/natural expression.

Jessica Martinez's confirmed travel to Japan (Tokyo) for work. Relevant travel facts: US citizens do not need a visa for tourism or business stays up to 90 days in Japan; proof of onward travel (e.g., return ticket) and possibly sufficient funds may be required. No required vaccinations for Japan, but CDC recommendations/routine vaccines should be current; Japan has lifted most COVID restrictions but requirements should be verified closer to travel. Jessica believes she's current on all routine vaccinations. She does not expect any name change and does not travel enough to need the larger 52-page passport book. She is interested in vegetarian/dietary meal options on flights and may pre-select meals closer to the trip.

Jessica Marie Martinez's personal details: full legal name (as it appears on her passport) is Jessica Marie Martinez, and her date of birth is March 8th, 1985. She works from home most days. Her work email is jmartinez@techcorp.com. Her company allows business class airfare for flights over 10 hours.

Jessica Martinez has a confirmed business trip to Tokyo, Japan for a conference, booked on Delta (confirmation number DELTA-JMK892). Outbound: DL 7, departs LAX at 11:30 AM on January 15th, arriving Haneda at 4:45 PM on January 16th. Return: DL 8, departs Haneda at 6:00 PM on January 22nd, arriving LAX at 10:15 AM the same day. She booked Business Class (total $4,890), which her company permits for flights over 10 hours (flight is ~11h15m westbound, ~10h15m eastbound). Seat 4A (window) on both legs. Business class is fully refundable if cancelled 24 hours before departure, with no change fees (fare difference may apply). Includes 2 free checked bags up to 70 lbs each, full meal service, complimentary wifi, and Sky Priority check-in/security. Delta uses Terminals 2 and 3 at LAX (international typically Terminal 2). She plans to handle her hotel booking separately.

Jessica Martinez's travel loyalty and credentials: Delta SkyMiles member number 2847569923 (the Tokyo trip will earn approx. 22,000 miles). She has a TSA PreCheck Known Traveler Number: 9988432. She prefers a window seat and dislikes waiting at airports.

Jessica Martinez pays for business travel using a corporate American Express card (billing zip code 90210) — e.g., she used it for her Tokyo flight. She also personally holds a Chase Sapphire Reserve (last four 8823, $25,000 limit), which she uses for travel and dining rewards, lounges, and travel insurance. Corporate booking details should be kept on file, though sensitive card credentials should not be stored in full.

Jessica Martinez has a Chase Sapphire Reserve credit card (last four digits 8823) with a $25,000 credit limit, currently using about $3,200. Benefits: no foreign transaction fees, chip and PIN capable for international use, and no travel notifications required before trips. Her statement closes on the 28th of each month, with payment due ~25 days later (around the 22nd of the following month). She has autopay set to pay the full balance from her Chase checking account. She also has a Chase debit card she can use at ATMs abroad.

Jessica Martinez's Chase Sapphire Reserve travel benefits (active as long as she pays for the travel with the card): trip cancellation up to $10,000, trip delay reimbursement, lost luggage coverage, and emergency medical; primary rental car coverage (decline the rental company's insurance); Priority Pass membership with 1,300+ lounges worldwide (up to 2 free guests per visit), plus access to Chase Sapphire Lounges (currently Boston, Hong Kong, and New York LaGuardia — not yet LAX). Note: her Tokyo flights are paid with her corporate AmEx, so the airline ticket itself isn't covered by Sapphire travel insurance, but hotels/other expenses paid with the Sapphire would be.

Jessica Martinez's Chase Sapphire Reserve rewards: earns 3x points on travel and dining worldwide (hotels, airlines, car rentals, trains, taxis, and rideshare like Uber count as travel) and 1x on everything else. Points are worth 1.5 cents each when redeemed through Chase Ultimate Rewards for travel (more when transferred to partners). Transfer partners include United, Southwest, JetBlue, Hyatt, Marriott, IHG, and several international airlines; Delta is not a direct partner but can be booked via Air France/KLM Flying Blue.

Jessica Martinez has several potential future work trips in addition to the confirmed Tokyo conference (Jan 15–22, 2025): she mentioned possibly traveling to Japan, Singapore, and London for work. She prefers to pay in local currency abroad and declines dynamic currency conversion (letting Visa do the conversion for better rates). In Japan, foreigner-friendly ATMs that work with Chase cards include 7-Eleven ATMs and Japan Post Bank ATMs.
